title: gpu-nodepool-tfmodules-reconcile-and-rollback-safe-state-pointer
author: Maya Patel
description: Problem: During Private upgrades we observed long-lived tfstate drift for GPU node pools caused by partial failures in nodepool creation and cross-account IAM role updates; rollbacks were error-prone because the existing tfstate layout pinned resources across tenant and infra boundaries. Motivation: make TF modules resilient to partial apply, enable a safe state-pointer rollback strategy, and reconcile nodepool leases to avoid orphaned GPU nodes and leaked IAM bindings. This PR introduces a set of changes across Terraform modules and helper tooling to allow idempotent reconciliation and safe rollback of Private deployments. Key changes: 1) module/gpu/nodepool: introduce a nodepool 'lease' resource that records allocation metadata in a tenant-scoped state pointer (short-lived state object) so nodepool creation can be reconciled without relying on global tfstate ordering; adds a reconcile script hook for the installer to attempt non-destructive repair on partial applies. 2) module/iam/gpu-roles: split role bindings into reusable, immutable role module and tenant-specific binding module; add cross-account assume-role policy migration helper to avoid transient deny windows during swap. 3) module/network/vpc: add nat-gateway tagging and route table reconciliation code; when NAT allocation fails during an upgrade the reconciler will mark routes as 'degraded' and attach a temporary egress path until rollback completes. 4) module/state/migrator: introduce a state-pointer migrator that can copy small, tenant-scoped pointers between tfstate backends (s3 -> gcs style) and an --atomic flag that attempts a safe two-phase swap. 5) cli/scripts/rollback-helper.sh: a guarded rollback tool that validates expected pointers and runs terraform state rm/apply operations in a preflight mode before doing destructive steps. Migration plan: non-breaking by default; installer will run the migrator in dry-run mode and surface diffs in console. Rollbacks: the rollback-helper creates a checkpointed copy of tenant pointers and verifies IAM role continuity before removing newly-created bindings. Testing: added unit-conftest policies for IAM, integration harness that runs a local minikube + mocked cloud backend (s3 emulator) to exercise partial apply and rollback flows. Backwards compatibility: modules expose an opt-in variable enable_state_pointers (default false) so clusters can migrate on a controlled cadence. Callouts: the migrator requires auxiliary permissions to read/write both source and target tfstate backends and to create temporary assume-role bindings during migration; these are documented in the README and the installer will surface clear error messages if permissions are lacking. Related: ENG-1423 implements the reconciler operator; SUP-881 surfaced the customer incident that motivated this work. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed - [x] migration scripts tested in staging - [x] revert/rollback verified via rollback-helper - [x] infra / security review completed

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can we avoid a second long-lived backend copy during migration? Suggest we keep tenant pointers small and do a streaming copy with checksum validation.
Maya Patel (author): Answered - migrator uses a small tenant pointer object (<= 8KB) and supports streaming copy; --atomic validated by checksum before swap.
Liam O'Connor: Security review - migrator needs temporary sts:AssumeRole to create temporary bindings; please add explicit audit log events in the README.
Maya Patel (author): Added audit logging notes and tightened permission guidance; reviewer requested a test showing permission failure is surfaced gracefully.
Priya Nair: Integration tests flaked on initial run due to emulator rate limits; re-ran with backoff and passed; approve pending small nit on variable naming.
Maya Patel: Renamed enable_state_pointers -> enable_state_pointers_for_migration to make intent clearer and updated README.
merge_notes: Merged after approvals from infra and security. Migration is behind opt-in flags; installer will enable in next staged rollout.
release_notes: Add opt-in tenant-scoped state pointers and a migrator + rollback helper to make Private TF upgrades resilient to partial failures; users must review migrator permissions before enabling.
notes_for_ops: Before enabling enable_state_pointers_for_migration=true in production, run the migrator in dry-run mode and ensure the installer account has cross-backend read/write and sts:AssumeRole permissions. Rollback flow creates a timestamped checkpoint in the same backend under 'migration_checkpoints/'.
